title: Part 5 Practice: Future Trends in Emerging Technologies

questions.text: Which of the following is listed as an emerging technology trend in 2019 according to the module?
options: A) Steam Engine
B) 5G Networks
C) Telegraph
D) Spinning Jenny
questions.explanation: Section 1.5.1 explicitly lists '5G Networks' as an emerging technology trend in 2019. The others are historical inventions from the Industrial Revolution.

questions.text: What does the module say about who emerging technologies affect?
options: A) They only affect the top 1% of tech geniuses at companies like Google.
B) They are already shaping your life whether you like it or not.
C) They will not affect society for another 50 years.
D) They are only relevant to businesses in the United States.
questions.correct_answer: B) They are already shaping your life whether you like it or not.
questions.explanation: The module debunks the myth: 'This is totally wrong. Chatbots, virtual/augmented reality, blockchain, Ephemeral Apps and Artificial Intelligence are already shaping your life whether you like it or not.'

questions.text: What is the final, powerful message of the module regarding technological change?
options: A) Avoid technology at all costs.
B) Adapt or die.
C) Wait for technology to mature before using it.
D) Technology is a passing fad.
questions.explanation: The module concludes with: 'At the end of the day, you can either adapt or die.'

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT listed as a future-shaping technology in section 1.5.2?
options: A) Chatbots
B) Virtual Reality (VR)
C) Blockchain
D) The Steam Engine
questions.explanation: Section 1.5.2 lists Chatbots, VR, Blockchain, Ephemeral Apps, and AI as technologies shaping the future. The Steam Engine is a historical invention (IR 1.0).

questions.text: What is an 'Ephemeral App' as described in the module?
options: A) An app that is permanently installed on your phone.
B) An app designed for temporary or short-term use, often disappearing after a specific task.
C) An app that requires no internet connection.
D) An app that is only used by large corporations.
questions.correct_answer: B) An app designed for temporary or short-term use, often disappearing after a specific task.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral Apps are listed in section 1.5.2 as a technology shaping the future. 'Ephemeral' implies temporary or short-lived, referring to apps used for a specific immediate purpose (like a festival event app).

questions.text: How is Blockchain being used in Ethiopia's coffee industry according to the lesson?
options: A) To mine cryptocurrency.
B) To track coffee supply chains, ensuring fair payments and authenticating Ethiopian coffee to global buyers.
C) To replace coffee farming with digital farming.
D) To create a new cryptocurrency called 'EthioCoin'.
questions.correct_answer: B) To track coffee supply chains, ensuring fair payments and authenticating Ethiopian coffee to global buyers.
questions.explanation: The lesson provides an Ethiopian example: 'Ethiopia's Ministry of Agriculture is piloting blockchain to track coffee supply chains, ensuring fair payments to farmers and proving the authenticity of Ethiopian coffee to global buyers.'

questions.text: Which technology is described as a 'decentralized, distributed ledger technology'?
options: A) Artificial Intelligence (AI)
B) Blockchain
C) 5G Networks
D) Digital Twins
questions.explanation: The table in section 1.5.1 describes Blockchain as 'A decentralized, distributed ledger technology that records transactions across multiple computers securely and transparently.'

questions.text: What is the purpose of 'Immersive Experiences in Smart Spaces'?
options: A) To replace all physical classrooms.
B) To combine AR, VR, and smart sensors to create interactive, immersive environments for retail, education, and entertainment.
C) To create 5G networks.
D) To build autonomous vehicles.
questions.correct_answer: B) To combine AR, VR, and smart sensors to create interactive, immersive environments for retail, education, and entertainment.
questions.explanation: The module describes 'Immersive Experiences in Smart Spaces' as combining AR, VR, and smart sensors to create interactive environments, used in smart retail, virtual classrooms, and entertainment.

questions.text: Which Ethiopian institution is mentioned as beginning to use VR for medical training?
options: A) Ethiopian Airlines
B) Addis Ababa University
C) Commercial Bank of Ethiopia
D) Ethio Telecom
questions.explanation: The lesson provides an example: 'Ethiopian universities like Addis Ababa University are beginning to use VR for medical training, allowing students to practice surgeries in a virtual environment before touching a real patient.'

questions.text: What is the core problem with the belief that emerging technologies only affect 'top tier' tech companies?
options: A) It is true; only big companies benefit.
B) It is wrong because these technologies are already shaping everyday lives, including chatbots, AI, and VR.
C) It is correct because only geniuses can use them.
D) It is a myth because emerging technologies only affect the government.
questions.correct_answer: B) It is wrong because these technologies are already shaping everyday lives, including chatbots, AI, and VR.
questions.explanation: The module explicitly states: 'This is totally wrong. Chatbots, virtual/augmented reality, blockchain, Ephemeral Apps and Artificial Intelligence are already shaping your life whether you like it or not.'
